items.title: What Blade Runner got wrong about AI (so far)
items.excerpt: Blade Runner promised rain, ziggurats and androids; the real machine arrived as a blank box to type into. The essay grades the film's design forecast and argues where AI interfaces are actually heading.
items.why: A designer-facing argument about what AI interfaces really look like — useful framing for anyone shipping AI UI.

items.title: Run Claude Managed Agents with Chat SDK
items.excerpt: Vercel's Chat SDK now supports Claude Managed Agents, so teams can wire a hosted coding/design agent straight into a chat UI without building the orchestration layer themselves.
items.why: Lowers the bar for design engineers to ship agent-driven product surfaces.

items.title: Build and deploy eve agents from the Vercel dashboard
items.excerpt: Agents can now be created, configured and deployed directly from the Vercel dashboard, no local scaffolding required.
items.why: Prompt-to-agent from a GUI puts agent building inside a designer's reach.

items.title: The best workflow engine is a programming language
items.excerpt: Vercel argues that durable AI workflows belong in ordinary code rather than in a bespoke visual workflow builder — a direct challenge to node-graph automation tools.
items.why: Reframes how creative/product teams should structure their AI automation stack.

items.title: Why AI Websites All Look the Same and How to Build Something Different
items.excerpt: A breakdown of why prompt-generated sites converge on the same gradient-and-card aesthetic, and the constraints, tokens and references that push AI output off the default.
items.why: AI slop homogenisation is the core craft problem for designers using generative UI tools.

items.title: Teaching AI Design: Golden Ratios & Modular UI Blocks in LuxurAI
items.excerpt: A build log on encoding classical proportion rules and modular block systems into an AI generator so its output follows design-system logic instead of guesswork.
items.why: Concrete method for making an AI obey design rules — the token/system-as-guardrail pattern.

items.title: Style Consistency Across AI Image Sets: The Prompt Habits That Make Ten Images Look Like One Brand
items.excerpt: Practical prompt discipline for holding one visual identity across a whole set of generated images rather than ten unrelated one-offs.
items.why: Brand consistency is the #1 blocker to shipping generative imagery in real campaigns.

items.title: How Tripo Is Tackling Clean Topology for its 3D Asset Pipeline
items.excerpt: Tripo co-founder Dr. Yanpei Cao explains Smart Mesh — generating usable, animation-ready topology in seconds — and the company's push from single assets toward complete interactive worlds.
items.why: Clean topology is the gate between AI 3D output and a real production pipeline.

items.title: The power of on-premises open-weight models for generative media
items.excerpt: Why studios are moving generative image and video work onto local open-weight models — control over data, IP and look, without sending client material to a cloud API.
items.why: On-prem generative media changes what creative studios can legally and safely ship.

items.title: Adobe just added a brand new AI-assisted editor to Photoshop
items.excerpt: Adobe appears to be fully embracing prompt-based editing in Photoshop with a new AI-assisted editor that takes written markup and instructions directly on the canvas.
items.why: Photoshop is the default surface for most visual designers; prompt-first editing changes daily craft.

items.title: The $3.4m Disney auction is a reminder of what AI concept art takes from us
items.excerpt: A record-breaking auction of original Disney concept art becomes an argument about what is lost when concept development collapses into a prompt.
items.why: The clearest current framing of AI's cost to concept-art craft and its market value.

items.title: "Unsettling" - Nvidia's controversial DLSS 5 AI filter has leaked, and gamers are horrified
items.excerpt: A leaked DLSS 5 AI filter that reinterprets rendered frames has drawn a backlash over how far generative post-processing should be allowed to alter an artist's intended image.
items.why: Real-time generative post-processing puts art direction in the hands of the GPU.

items.title: Google further buries search results under AI mode
items.excerpt: Google is auto-expanding AI Overviews so generated answers push traditional blue links further down the page, reshaping how any designed web page gets discovered.
items.why: Changes the distribution reality for every website designers build.

items.title: Hugging Face's new robot is an adorable rollerskating duck
items.excerpt: Hugging Face's open-source MicroDuck is a small rollerskating robot aimed at makers — an open hardware platform for embodied AI experiments.
items.why: Cheap open embodied-AI hardware is where physical product designers can start prototyping.

items.title: Google's AI note-taking app now allows you to interact with books
items.excerpt: Google's notebook app adds expert sources including full books, letting research grounding come from vetted material rather than scraped web pages.
items.why: Better-grounded AI research changes the discovery phase of design work.

items.title: OpenAI will pull its models from Cursor due to SpaceXAI acquisition
items.excerpt: OpenAI plans to cut off Cursor's access to its models on November 12, 2026, forcing everyone who prototypes UI in Cursor onto a different model lineup.
items.why: Directly changes the model options inside the IDE many design engineers ship from.

items.title: Sony and Warner sue Anthropic for 'blatant violation' of copyright law
items.excerpt: Music publishing groups allege thousands of instances of copyright infringement, escalating the legal fight over what creative material AI models may be trained on.
items.why: Training-data rulings set the ground rules for what creatives can legally generate and ship.

items.title: Enterprise AI's real risk isn't autonomous agents. It's the complexity between them.
items.excerpt: The hard problem is not a single rogue agent but the unpredictable interactions between many agents cascading through an organisation's systems and handoffs.
items.why: Design orgs adding agents to their workflow inherit exactly this handoff problem.

items.title: Meta researchers taught an 8B AI model to match Claude Opus 4.5 - without the frontier price tag
items.excerpt: Meta's EvoHarness-RL trains an 8B model to manage its own workspace and tool use, matching Claude Opus 4.5 on agentic tasks at a fraction of the cost.
items.why: Cheap small models make always-on agents affordable inside design tooling.

items.title: Shadow agents make the old shadow IT problem worse
items.excerpt: Teams are spinning up unsanctioned AI agents faster than IT can inventory them, recreating shadow IT with far more autonomy attached.
items.why: Design teams building their own agents are the shadow-agent problem — governance is coming.

items.title: Atomica introduces AI Thermal Microstructures Platform
items.excerpt: Atomica launched a platform for AI-designed thermal microstructures, applying generative methods to the physical geometry of heat-management components.
items.why: Generative geometry moving into real manufacturable hardware design.

items.title: Mastercam and ProShop partner on connected manufacturing workflows
items.excerpt: A CAM and ERP integration that keeps design intent, tooling and shop-floor data connected across the manufacturing chain.
items.why: Design-to-manufacture handoff automation for product/industrial designers.

items.title: My agent army writes Code Connect | Dev Mindset
items.excerpt: A Figma engineer runs a fleet of coding agents to generate Code Connect mappings, showing what it looks like to supervise agents instead of writing the glue code yourself.
items.why: Concrete demo of the design-system-to-code handoff being done by agents.

items.title: The Billion Dollar AI Gap Is Collapsing
items.excerpt: Two Minute Papers walks through how quickly open and small models are closing on frontier systems, and what that means for anyone building on top of them.
items.why: If cheap models match frontier ones, creative tools get frontier quality by default.
